correctness.rationale: OU variance solves v(t)=(D/lambda)[1-(1-c)e^(-2lambda t)], so endpoint Jeffreys divergence is F_c(x)/(2c) with F=(u-c)^2/u. Verified symbolic first and second derivatives; H_c(u)=2c²-c²u-u³ strictly decreases from positive to negative for c<u<1, producing one inflection. Q=xF'-F has one positive zero z_c after that point, yielding unique global tangent from origin and the least concave majorant equal to linear up to z_c then F. Jensen and equality/contact analysis give the exact two-regime supremum, deterministic uniqueness for mu>=tc, and strict-positive nonattainment below tc. Taylor/implicit-function expansion near c=0 gives zc=sqrt(2c)-c/3+O(c^1.5), normalized rate; independent numerical roots support it. Complete theorem rests on analysis, not finite checks.
